stories.title: US renews strikes on Iran after military personnel killed
stories.summary: The United States has said it completed an eighth straight night of attacks against Iran after earlier announcing that two US military personnel were killed in Jordan and another was missing following an Iranian ⁠assault. The US and Iran have intensified attacks since an interim ceasefire deal signed a month ago fell apart last week, raising the possibility of a return to all-out war. US Central Command said in a statement that the airstrikes began at 6pm ET Saturday (11pm Irish time), at President Donald Trump's direction. "The strikes are designed to further degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and swiftly punish Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces who launched attacks against American service members in Jordan last night," it said.

stories.title: Tate brothers arrested in US in relation to UK inquiry
stories.summary: Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan have been arrested in the United States in connection with a UK police investigation into a number of alleged sexual offences, Bedfordshire Police has said. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said it was bringing further charges against the brothers - who were arrested by US Marshals in Miami - in relation to allegations from four additional victims. The CPS said it has requested the extradition of the brothers from the US. Social media influencer Andrew Tate, 39, is charged with seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and 19 additional charges for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

stories.title: Russian missiles strike Kyiv killing one, wounding 13
stories.summary: Russian missiles struck the Ukrainian capital Kyiv and the surrounding region early today, killing ⁠at least one person and wounding 13 others as fires broke out across the city, officials said. A series of powerful explosions thundered in the night, as Ukraine's air force warned of a ballistic missile threat. Fires broke out at a dormitory, an apartment building and a supermarket, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko ‌said on the ⁠Telegram app. Several non-residential buildings and warehouses were struck in the attack, while parked cars and office buildings were onfire in several districts, Mr Klitschko said.

stories.title: New Athlone addiction service as gambling issues rise
stories.summary: A new outpatient addiction service unit has been launched in Athlone, Co Westmeath due to increased demand for treatment from the west of the country, particularly those affected by gambling. The Rutland Centre, which runs a specialist addiction treatment service in Knocklyon in Dublin, is introducing a second outpatient service to the midlands. The new service responds to growing demand from people who previously faced lengthy journeys to Dublin to access treatment. Karl Fitzharris, treatment co-ordinator for the new Athlone programme, said: "For too long, we've had to turn away people who desperately wanted treatment because travelling to Dublin twice a week simply wasn't practical."

stories.title: Consumers facing winter of discontent amid soaring prices
stories.summary: Consumers have been hit by repeated price shocks across the board over the past few years; punctuated by multiple energy price hikes, the rising cost of food, and more recently a spike in fuel prices. And with the increases showing no sign of relenting, before the year is out they could be paying even more at fuel pumps, on energy bills, and at supermarket check-outs. Just before the US began its strikes on Iran at the end of February, a barrel of brent crude oil (the industry benchmark) was costing around $73. But two months of sustained conflict in the Middle East saw oil spike to $114 a barrel in May, before falling back below $72 at the start of this month - while now it's hovering near the $85 a barrel mark.

stories.title: Galway puzzle will test Limerick's final-winning habit
stories.summary: Today's game is the fourth All-Ireland final meeting of Galway and Limerick. The second was 1980, played, coincidentally, in 1980. By rights, Joe Connolly could have begun his speech with "Tár éis sé bliain agus caoga..." The third was 2018, the match which commenced this incredible run in finals for John Kiely and set their greatest generation on their way. It almost feels like another world now. Kiely was in his second year in charge. His first had been highly unpromising, so much so that it almost feels like it belongs to someone else's managerial tenure.
